title: capacity-prepositioning-readout-west-asia-2026-03-15
content:
Purpose
-----
Weekly readout from the infra capacity sync focusing on prepositioning GPUs for an upcoming model release and traffic shift toward APAC. Goal: summarize the risk posture, actions taken this week, short-term mitigations, and owners for next steps.

Context and trigger
-------------------
- Product plans to roll out model v2.1 (larger context window, ~1.6x per-token cost) starting 2026-03-20 in staged fashion across hosted API and Dedicated pools.
- Expected traffic uplift in APAC (asia-east1, asia-northeast1) due to a partner launch; estimated 30–45% increase in peak RPS for conversational endpoints serving that partner.
- Current fleet mix: H100 (reserved, asia-east1), A100-40GB (us-west1, reserved + spot mix), A10G/RTX6000 for burst capacity in europe.

Observed signals this week
-------------------------
- Baseline: average token throughput across affected routes 1.2M tokens/s; peak 2.9M tokens/s (us-west1 + asia-east1).
- Telemetry shows 12% higher median latency on <region=asia-east1, model=base-v1> during evening hours (UTC+8) compared to last week.
- Two node retirements unexpectedly reduced usable H100 capacity by ~8% in asia-east1 (one HW failure, one maintenance).
- Spot pool churn in us-west1 spiked after cloud provider(s) reclaimed capacity; autoscaler oscillation observed on 2026-03-13 leading to transient queueing.

Risk matrix (quick)
-------------------
- Capacity shortfall (probability: medium-high): can cause increased tail latency and fallback to smaller model variants.
- Cost spike (probability: medium): pre-warming & reserve bursts will add to short-term cost.
- Regional imbalance (probability: high if unmitigated): degraded user experience for APAC customers.

Actions completed this week
-------------------------
1) Pre-reserved 12 H100 GPUs in asia-east1 for 2026-03-19 to 2026-04-02 window (contracted via Dedicated burst quota). Owner: Marco Alvarez.
2) Deployed autoscaler tuning PR to reduce oscillation: increased min-pool-size, smoothed scale-down window from 60s -> 300s. PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/489. Owner: Xiaoyu Chen.
3) Hot-warm cache pre-warming script (kv-warm) tested and scheduled — seeds top 200 prompt prefixes into KV cache for partner traffic profile. Runs daily at 02:00 UTC. Owner: Priya Nambiar.
4) Launched a targeted canary routing rule: new-traffic to model-v2.1 will start on a single AZ in asia-east1 and fall back to model-v1 on overload. Config change: rollout-config/2026-03-14. Owner: Sienna Patel.

Short-term mitigations (next 7 days)
-----------------------------------
- Priority 1: Run a 4-hour evacuation drill in asia-east1 (simulate losing an AZ). Measure failover times and eviction impact on latency. Target date: 2026-03-17 01:00–05:00 UTC. Lead: Liam O'Connor.
- Priority 2: Hold spot pool cap at 20% of burst capacity to avoid excessive churn-induced autoscaler oscillations. Implement via quota guard rails. Lead: Xiaoyu Chen.
- Priority 3: Increase KV cache TTL for partner keys to 6 hours during the launch window. Owner: Priya Nambiar.
- Priority 4: Enable cross-region read routing (us-west1 -> asia-edge) for low-latency read-only embedding lookups; monitor SLOs closely. Owner: Marco Alvarez.

Operational runbook edits proposed
--------------------------------
- Add a new checklist "APAC prepositioning" that includes validation steps: reserved capacity check, prewarm verification, fallback routing smoke tests, quota confirmations with cloud provider contacts. Draft PR: runbooks/apac-prepositioning.md.
- Add metric thresholds for autoscaler hysteresis to avoid oscillation: scale-down-cooldown >= 300s, min-healthy-instances >= 2 per AZ.

Open questions / decisions needed
--------------------------------
- How long should we keep reserved H100s beyond initial two-week window? Cost estimate attached in linked sheet; decision needed by 2026-03-18. Request: Ops leadership approval for extended burst until 2026-04-15 if adoption metrics justify.
- Should we temporarily restrict model-v2.1 rollout to Dedicated customers only for the first 48 hours to limit production risk? Product input required.

Metrics & checkpoints to watch
------------------------------
- 95th/99th token latency on partner routes (target: <= 120ms / <= 250ms respectively).
- Token throughput per region normalized by reserved GPUs.
- Autoscaler scaling events per hour (target: < 3 per hour during peak).
- KV cache hit rate for seeded prefixes (target: > 80% within 2 hours of prewarm run).

Owners & action list (short)
---------------------------
- Marco Alvarez: Confirm extended reservation approval timeline, set up billing alerts. Due: 2026-03-18.
- Xiaoyu Chen: Merge autoscaler tuning, enforce spot cap, update runbook. Due: 2026-03-16.
- Priya Nambiar: Deploy kv-warm to prod schedule, validate hit rates post-run. Due: 2026-03-16.
- Liam O'Connor: Lead evacuation drill, publish drill report. Due: 2026-03-18.
- Sienna Patel: Complete rollout rule docs and canary dashboard. Due: 2026-03-16.

Post-mitigation plan (if shortfall persists)
------------------------------------------
- Activate rollback plan: pause model-v2.1 rollout, throttle partner traffic at edge with rate-limiting, and revert to model-v1 for Dedicated fallback.
- If cost becomes prohibitive, switch reserved H100s to on-demand H100s for short bursts and rely more on A100 fallback for steady-state.

Notes & miscellany
------------------
- Slack ops channel: #infra-capacity; escalate via @oncall-infra for urgent capacity events.
- Reminder: update the public status page only after customer-impacting degradations are confirmed.

Appendix (short numbers)
-----------------------
- Current reserved H100s (asia-east1): 48 total, 4 offline for maintenance -> usable 44.
- Planned burst reservation: +12 (-> usable 56 for launch window).
- Estimated incremental tokens/s need for partner peak: +600k tokens/s. Each H100 provisioned in our stack supports ~40k tokens/s for the load profile; 600k / 40k = ~15 H100-equivalents needed. Our +12 reservation covers most, remainder covered by A100 mixed pool with expected latency tradeoff.

If anything looks off in the numbers or you want a deeper simulation (cost vs latency tradeoff across different mix scenarios), I can run the monte-carlo capacity simulator on the linked sheet — ask in thread or add to INFRA-2345.

-- Priya Nambiar (infra capacity lead)
